stored.fact: Call in internal/memory/claude.go represents one isolated structured Claude Code request.
When Call.MCPConfig is set, it is inline --mcp-config JSON naming the only MCP servers the call may use.
When Call.MCPConfig is set, Call.AllowedTools lists the only tools the call may call.
Call.Tools, when set, lists the built-in read-only file tools the call may use, confined to its temp dir.
Call.Files seeds the temp dir that confines the call's built-in tools.
Call.MaxTurns caps the tool loop via --max-turns; 0 leaves the cap off.
The Runner interface runs one Call and returns the structured_output object.
Result is a finished call: the structured_output plus what Claude Code reported spending.
CLIRunner drives the claude CLI headless with all ambient context switched off.
Under CLIRunner, only our system prompt and the stdin document are visible to the model.
claudeArgs does not use --bare, because --bare forces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY auth and never reads OAuth/keychain, which breaks a subscription login.
For tool calls, --restricted confines Read and Grep to the working dir and drops code-running tools.
Without --restricted, Read opened an absolute path outside cwd under --safe-mode (probed in P274).
--safe-mode disables --mcp-config servers too (measured in P211), so an MCP call runs without it.
--strict-mcp-config still keeps every other MCP server out.
CLIRunner.Available reports whether the claude CLI can be found.
CLIRunner.RunResult is Run plus the cost and turn count that Claude Code reports.
